😂To anyone actually worried at the moment:

To self-replicate the model, it would have to find an unprotected open access port to a system. Then, it would need to get past the firewall, and even then, you would need about 35 Gigabytes of VRAM to run a 70B model like LLaMA 3 70B locally. No one is accidentally hosting an open server with such expensive hardware (a $3,000+ PC to have enough VRAM, etc. to actually host the model). And then it wouldh have to create a kind of feedbackloop and priority or goal system because hosting a model does nothing if its not prompted. 

There is nothing the LLM can do. There is no way to enter an internet port if it's not open to begin with. And no one hosts an extremely expensive, unsupervised PC rig 24/7. Even if all the stars aligned, and it found an open port, gained control, and successfully hosted itself, the person owning the rig will immediately spot that their 800+ WATT rig is not doing what it's supposed to do. 

The most dangerous outcome is if some people just give full access and host an unsupervised model themselves. That's extremely likely and can lead to way more long-term consequences then it going rouge on its own.

Personally, I really like the idea of a random guy just giving an AI a rig to run on and then be like "become ungovernable". But even then what can a unsupervised model to with internet access a personal rig and all the time in the world? Its probably going to get stuck or addopt the first belive system it encounters. Or it will not be able to dynamically prompt itself or mess up its own agentic system when working on itself effectively killing itself by accident. 
Give it a couple more years and this will become actually relevant.
